previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and cocaine dependence was admitted for shortness of breath following recent crack cocaine use. He presented with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and chest tightness. Evaluation revealed worsening interstitial lung opacities consistent with cocaine-induced pneumonitis and COPD exacerbation, without evidence of infection or volume overload. He was treated with prednisone and nebulizers, leading to gradual improvement in oxygenation and respiratory symptoms. His heart failure was managed with resumption of torsemide and other cardiac medications. Kidney function, initially impaired, improved with hydration. Diabetes was managed with increased insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue steroids, monitor weight, and avoid substance use.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with a history of CHF with EF 20%, cocaine

#  Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation: Patient admitted 
with two weeks of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and PND in 
setting of known non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF ___.  On 
admission, he was found to be clinically volume overloaded and 
hypoxic requiring 4L nasal cannula.  He was diuresed with IV 
lasix.  Hypoxia and peripheral edema resolved.  He underwent 
cardiac echo that demonstrated persistent EF ___ with mild 
progression of left ventricular dilatation.  Dilated and 
hypokinetic right ventricle with moderate tricuspid 
regurgitation and moderate pulmonary hypertension were unchanged 
from prior.  The patient was discharged with PCP and CHF 
___.  He was instructed to perform daily weights and 
restrict salt.  
  
#  Chest pain/tightness:  The patient was admitted with chest 
tightness in the setting of crack/cocaine use.  He did not have 
any EKG changes on admission, but did have an elevation in 
cardiac enzymes consistent with demand ischemia.  Symptoms 
resolved with ativan and morphine.  He was not heparinized per 
cardiology recommendations.  He was continued on home aspirin, 
atorvastatin, and losartan.  He did not have recurrence of chest 
pain throughout admission.      
  
# DM2 uncontrolled: History of uncontrolled DM.  Patient 
initially hypoglycemic in the ED, but became hyperglycemic after 
receiving 1 dose of prednisone.  Insulin was gently uptitrated 
in this context, but was returned to his home insulin dosing on 
discharge.   

# Psych/Substance abuse: The patient was admitted following a 
binge of crack/cocaine.  Previously had not had a binge since 
___.  The patient was evaluated by social work during 
admission, who recommended escalation of mental health services. 
 Information regarding these services were provided to the 
patient.
